review_notes: Walls safety -1/medium is the same call as Tse (NE Pos 1) and Rose-Akins (West Pos 1): a prosecution-only formation (26 years, self-reported [S1][S3]) and no bail, sentencing or therapeutic-court statements. Her youth-diversion community board seat [S3] is too thin to pull the score to 0, and medium properly reflects that the score rests on formation, not stated positions. Walls experience -1/medium: the 'unmatched 26-year record' quote in the basis appears in her pamphlet statement (checked against the local-edition text behind [S1]). Her 17 years pro tem are also self-reported. Merfeld safety +1/medium is his own explicit platform: more access to therapeutic courts for people who could benefit, a treatment role for the court in the fentanyl response [S4], and a formation in both prosecution and defense [S3]. 'Will impose jail when the facts... show that it is necessary' [S4] correctly holds it at +1. This matches Masaniai (SW Pos 4) and Martin (West Pos 1). Merfeld experience +1/medium was the weakest score. He is a career criminal and dependency lawyer, not an outsider, and his 'community engagement' pitch is about judicial approach, not generational change. But the axis measures profile, and he has no judicial or pro tem service against an opponent with 17 years pro tem [S1][S3]. That is the same profile and score as Harris (SE Pos 5, +1/medium), so it stands. The basis wording 'running on community engagement' would be better as 'no reported judicial or pro tem service'. Judicial is correctly omitted for both. Walls's materials are temperament boilerplate. Merfeld's pairs restraint ('Judges are not policymakers...') with access-to-justice and community-engagement themes [S4], which nets to at most a low-confidence 0, so no proposal. No score uses the 34th LD endorsement or the disputed 33rd LD claim. Copy flags: (1) Merfeld highlight 4 says he 'Supports court facilitators'. The dossier quote is 'considering the use of court facilitators' [S4]. Suggest 'Supports considering court facilitators for self-represented litigants'. (2) Both summaries state careers as fact ('Municipal prosecutor for South King County cities for 26 years'; 'previously a prosecutor in Okanogan County and a public defender...'), while both dossiers say the roles are self-reported and unconfirmed [S3]. The highlights hedge them; the summaries should too, or say 'reports'. (3) Walls highlight 3 lists the 34th District Democrats among her endorsers, and Merfeld's highlights mention no endorsements. That is factual, but consider also noting that both claim the 33rd LD Democrats, or dropping party organizations from the highlight. (4) The race_blurb's 'backed by most of the District Court bench' comes from her own endorsements page [S4]. Chief Judge Robertson appears on it and also endorses in SW Pos 4, so 'lists most of the District Court bench among her endorsers' would be more precise.
